# Synthetic fixtures

Small synthetic scores that exercise one notation feature each, plus two combined stress scores. They are generated, not hand-engraved: regenerate everything with

    ~/.venvs/MuseClaude/bin/python -I tools/fixtures/build_fixtures.py

(needs the built agent app at `agent.install/mscore.app`; pass `--only NAME` for one fixture, `--list` to list them). Every score is the app's own output: the generators write MusicXML, or an edited .mscx where MusicXML cannot express the feature, and the built app converts and re-saves it. Nothing here comes from `tests/fixtures/real/`.

Each line: file, what it exercises. *Produced*: how. *Verified*: the check run by the generator after every build, on top of the checks all fixtures get (open and re-save with `mscore -o` without `-f`, same element counts after re-save, export to MusicXML and parse with music21 + ElementTree).

- `chord-symbols.mscz` — Lead sheet with chord symbols: major, minor-7, dominant, maj7, slash chords (A and D bass, flat root, F#), add9, 7b9, min-maj7, sus4, 6/9, dim7, augmented, half-diminished, "N.C.", and a chord change in the middle of a held whole note. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (`<harmony>` with root, kind, bass, degree, offset), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* Re-exported MusicXML harmony list (root, kind, bass) equals the source in order; mscx holds the same number of `<Harmony>` elements.
- `cross-staff-beaming.mscz` — Piano with cross-staff beams: right-hand arpeggio whose low notes sit on the left-hand staff, left hand reaching up, a two-level sixteenth figure alternating staves, and a crossing pair. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (a voice's notes carry `<staff>` 1 or 2 plus explicit beams), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* mscx has `<staffMove>` on exactly the notes moved; re-exported MusicXML keeps one voice on both staffs and puts notes of both staffs in the same beam group.
- `grace-notes.mscz` — Grace notes before and after the beat: acciaccatura (slashed eighth), appoggiatura (plain eighth), groups of two 16th and three 32nd graces, graces before a chord and a grace chord, and graces after the last note of a bar. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (`<grace/>` with and without slash; graces written after the main note are the "after" ones), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* mscx: counts of acciaccatura / appoggiatura / grace16 / grace32 / grace16after chords match; re-exported MusicXML has the same number of `<grace>` notes and the after-graces follow their note.
- `irregular-bars.mscz` — Irregular (actual-duration) bars in 4/4: a bar of 3/4, a bar of 5/8, an overfull bar of 6/4, a bar split in two halves (second half excluded from the count), and a 1/8 bar. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (measures whose content differs from the time signature), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* mscx: the `<Measure len=...>` attributes are exactly [-, 3/4, 5/8, 6/4, 2/4, 2/4, 1/8, -] and the split half carries the irregular flag.
- `jumps-markers.mscz` — Navigation markers and jumps: segno (bar 3), "To Coda" (5), "D.S. al Coda" (6), coda sign (7), "Fine" (11) and "D.C. al Fine" (12), with a rehearsal mark and a tempo mark in bar 1. *Produced:* MusicXML skeleton from tools/fixtures/mxl.py through `mscore -o`; the Marker and Jump measure elements are then inserted into the .mscx by tools/fixtures/mscxedit.py (the MusicXML importer turns `<segno/>`, `<coda/>` and `<sound dalsegno=...>` into plain staff text, not real markers) and the app re-saves the file. *Verified:* mscx: Marker labels segno/coda/codab/fine and Jump texts sit on exactly the intended bars, and the jump targets are segno->coda->codab and start->fine.
- `key-time-changes.mscz` — Violin and cello through 15 bars of key and time changes: 4/4 C, G major (bar 3), 3/4 (4), Eb major and 6/8 together (6), 5/4 (8), F# minor (9), common time symbol (10), cut time + D minor (11), 7/8 (12), back to C major (13), 4/4 (14); cello clef changes bass-tenor-treble-bass. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (`<key>`, `<time>`, `<clef>` in later measures), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* Re-exported MusicXML: for both parts the (bar, key fifths, mode, beats/beat-type, symbol) changes and the cello clef changes equal the source exactly.
- `lyrics-melismas-verses.mscz` — Vocal line with three verses (verse 3 only in the first two bars), hyphenated two- and three-syllable words (begin/middle/end), and melismas drawn as extender lines over several notes, one of them running across a barline, with a slur over each melisma. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (`<lyric number>` with syllabic/text/extend), `mscore -o`. The words are invented filler, not from any song. *Verified:* Re-exported MusicXML: per verse the (text, syllabic) sequence equals the source and the two melisma lines start on the right syllables (`<extend/>`); mscx has one `<Lyrics>` per syllable and `<ticks_f>` 3/4 and 4/4 on the two melisma starts.
- `parts-linked.mscz` — Linked parts: a flute / B-flat clarinet / bassoon master (ties, slur, dynamic, staff text, chord, transposing clarinet) with three part scores (excerpts) linked to it: Flute, Clarinet in Bb, and a two-staff "Flute and Clarinet" part. The bassoon has no part. *Produced:* Master from MusicXML through `mscore -o`; the three excerpt scores are generated from the master's .mscx by tools/fixtures/excerpts.py (copied staves, new EIDs, `<linkedTo>` the master element), zipped into the same .mscz, and the app opens and re-saves the file. *Verified:* After the app re-save: three `Excerpts/*.mscx` exist with the right names; every `<linkedTo>` in them names an EID present in the master; every note in every part is linked; the part scores hold the same pitches as their master staves; the clarinet part keeps its transposition.
- `pickup-bar.mscz` — Pickup (anacrusis) bar: a one-quarter bar 0 in 3/4, six full bars, and a short final bar that completes the pickup. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (`<measure number="0" implicit="yes">`, short last bar), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* mscx: first `<Measure>` has len=1/4 and the irregular (excluded from count) flag, last has len=2/4; music21 on the export: measure 0 is one quarter long, the next bar starts at offset 1, numbers run 0..7.
- `pickup-bar-compound.mscz` — Pickup bar in compound time: 6/8 in G with a two-eighth pickup, and a second, mid-piece short bar (four eighths, excluded from the count) after a double barline. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py, `mscore -o`. *Verified:* mscx: first Measure len=2/8 (two eighths) with the irregular flag; the mid-piece short bar has len=4/8 and the irregular flag; no other measure carries a len.
- `repeats-voltas.mscz` — Repeats and voltas in ten 4/4 bars: a plain repeat with first and second endings (bars 1-4), a repeat played three times (5-6) running straight into another repeat (7-9, an end-start repeat barline), an ending labelled "1, 2" and a third ending, then a final barline. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (`<barline>` with `<repeat>`/`<ending>`, `times="3"`), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* mscx: start-repeat flags on bars 1/5/7, end-repeat counts (2, 3, 2) on bars 3/6/8, and Volta spanners with endings "1", "2", "1,2", "3" starting on bars 3/4/8/9; re-exported MusicXML has the same repeat directions and ending numbers (1, 2, "1, 2", 3).
- `spanners-system-break.mscz` — Spanners that cross forced system breaks (new system at bars 4, 7 and 10 of 12): two slurs (one running over three breaks), crescendo and diminuendo hairpins, an 8va line, a pedal line on the left-hand staff, a trill line, a "rit." text line, a glissando between bars 3 and 4, and two voltas, the first split by a break. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (slur, wedge, octave-shift, pedal, wavy-line, bracket, glissando, ending, `<print new-system>`), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* Re-exported MusicXML: every spanner starts and stops in the bars given; each one (except the second volta) straddles at least one system break; mscx has LayoutBreak on bars 3/6/9 and lists the spanner types present.
- `stress-combined.mscz` — Stress score 1: 41 bars (pickup + 40) for voice, Bb trumpet, Eb alto sax, piano and cello mixing everything: pickup bar and two irregular bars (2/4 in 3/4, 3/4 in 4/4); time changes 4/4, 3/4, 6/8, 5/4, 4/4 and key changes C, G, Eb, D minor, C; repeat with first/second endings; segno, To Coda, D.S. al Coda, coda; tuplets 3:2, 5:4, 2:3, 7:8, 9:8, 13:8 and a nested triplet; four voices on a piano staff; cross-staff beamed arpeggios; two lyric verses with a melisma; chord symbols; acciaccatura, appoggiatura, 32nd graces and graces after a note; ties over barlines and over system breaks; slur, hairpin, 8va, pedal and trill lines (slur, hairpin, 8va and a tie cross forced system breaks at bars 5, 13, 21, 29, 37); transposing trumpet and sax; cello clef changes. *Produced:* tools/fixtures/fx_combined.py: MusicXML via mxl.py -> `mscore -o`; the nested-tuplet bar (cello, bar 13) and the Marker/Jump elements are written into the .mscx by mscxedit.py; app re-save. *Verified:* Counts taken from the source and compared with the file / the MusicXML export: bars and bar lengths, time and key changes, tuplet ratios and nesting, voices, cross-staff chords, lyrics per verse, harmony count, grace kinds, repeats/voltas, markers/jumps, tie pairs, spanner bars straddling breaks, transposition, clef changes.
- `stress-dense-rhythms.mscz` — Stress score, one staff, 32 bars of dense rhythm: 4/4, 3/4, 7/8, 5/8, 9/16, 12/8, 3/2, 2/2, 6/8 and 5/4; 128th to half notes with up to double dots; 11 tuplet ratios (2:3 to 13:8) with rests inside; nested tuplets in three bars; chords; grace notes; ties across barlines; a second voice in eight bars. *Produced:* tools/fixtures/fx_dense.py: seeded random cells (MusicXML via mxl.py) -> `mscore -o`; the three nested-tuplet bars are written into the .mscx by mscxedit.py; app re-save. *Verified:* Source counts compared with the file: chord+rest count, the multiset of tuplet (actual, normal, base) in the mscx, ties, and the set of note values; every exported bar and voice sums to its time signature; 8 bars carry a second voice.
- `ties-barlines.mscz` — Ties across barlines: a single note, a whole chord, a three-bar chain (tie in and out of the same note), a chord with only one note tied on, dotted tied values inside a bar, and a tie over a time-signature change. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (`<tie>` + `<tied>`), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* Re-exported MusicXML: the tie pairs (start bar, stop bar, pitch) match exactly; mscx has one `<Tie>` spanner per pair.
- `ties-system-break.mscz` — Ties that cross forced system breaks and a forced page break: a single note over a system break, a three-bar chain over a break, a three-note chord over a page break. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (`<print new-system>` / `new-page` on the bar after the tie starts), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* mscx: LayoutBreak line after bars 3 and 7, page after bar 11 (i.e. new system/page starts bars 4, 8, 12); re-exported MusicXML tie pairs match and the tied bars straddle each break.
- `transposing-instruments.mscz` — Transposing instruments playing the same concert-pitch line (C4 up to C5, then Bb F# Eb Ab, then C and G): Bb trumpet, F horn, Eb alto sax, Bb tenor sax (sounds a major ninth below written), A clarinet, with a non-transposing flute as reference. Written pitches and key signatures are the transposed ones. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (`<transpose>` diatonic/chromatic/octave-change in each part, written pitches computed by fxutil.written), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* mscx: every staff's notes have the same concert `<pitch>` values; each Instrument has the expected transposeDiatonic/transposeChromatic; the exported MusicXML carries the same `<transpose>` totals per part.
- `tuplets-nested.mscz` — Nested tuplets: triplet in triplet, triplet in quintuplet, quintuplets in a duplet, three levels deep, nested with a chord and rests, sextuplet in quintuplet, two sibling nested groups. *Produced:* Single-staff MusicXML skeleton with whole-bar rests through `mscore -o`; the seven bars are then written into the .mscx by tools/fixtures/mscxedit.py (MuseScore's MusicXML importer cannot build nested tuplets, see "Things the fixtures showed" below) and the app re-saves the result. *Verified:* the fixture's own .mscx is walked (`<Tuplet>`/`<endTuplet/>`) and every chord/rest must carry the expected stack of ratios (up to 3 deep); 18 `<Tuplet>` elements; the MusicXML export still sums to 4/4 per bar.
- `tuplets-ratios.mscz` — One 4/4 bar per tuplet ratio: 2:3 (duplet), 3:2, 4:3, 5:4, 6:4, 7:4, 7:8, 8:6, 9:8, 10:8, 11:8, 12:8, 13:8, plus 3:2 on quarters, 5:4 on eighths, 3:2 on halves, and a 6/8 bar of two 2:3 duplets. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (time-modification + tuplet start/stop), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* mscx has the 18 `<Tuplet>` elements with exactly these actual/normal/base values in order; re-exported MusicXML notes carry the same ratio sequence.
- `tuplets-rests-ties-voices.mscz` — Tuplets that start with a rest or contain rests, a tie into a tuplet from the previous bar, out of a tuplet, and inside one, a tuplet of chords, and two voices at once carrying different ratios (3:2 against 5:4, 7:4 over straight eighths). *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py, `mscore -o`. *Verified:* Re-exported MusicXML: ratio sequence per voice per bar matches, the tie pairs (bar, bar, pitch) match, voice 2 exists in bars 5-6.
- `voices-four.mscz` — Four voices on one treble staff: four different rhythms at once, rests and a whole-bar rest in voice 4, triplets, a tie and chords in separate voices, then all four voices in whole notes. *Produced:* MusicXML from tools/fixtures/mxl.py (`<voice>` 1-4 with `<backup>`), `mscore -o`. *Verified:* mscx bars 1-4 each contain four `<voice>` elements; re-exported MusicXML has voices 1-4 in the same staff with the right note counts per voice per bar.

## Not produced, why

- Grace notes after a note in the middle of a bar — MusicXML has no way to say "after"; MuseScore's importer gives a grace note written after a note, with another note following in the bar, to the next chord (tested: it came out as a `grace16` before the next note). grace-notes.mscz therefore has after-graces only at the end of a bar, which the importer does turn into `grace16after`. A mid-bar "after" grace would need .mscx editing.
- Part-specific differences in linked parts (unlinked elements, per-part layout/style/visibility, "exclude from other parts", independent staff text) — parts-linked.mscz holds only fully linked content. The excerpt writer copies master staves, so anything that differs per part would be invented rather than produced by the app, and could not be verified as a state MuseScore itself reaches. Needs a part made and edited in the GUI (or a later fixture produced through the agent's own part commands).
- Golden export files (tests/golden/) — outside the paths this task may change (tests/fixtures/synthetic/ and tools/fixtures/); the round-trip MusicXML the generator exports for each check is thrown away with the work directory.

## Things the fixtures showed about MuseScore

- MuseScore's MusicXML importer cannot build nested tuplets: it takes the combined `<time-modification>` (e.g. 9:4 for a triplet inside a triplet) as one flat tuplet and pads the bar with rests; the app's own nested export does not re-import either. Nested tuplets in the corpus (`tuplets-nested`, three bars of `stress-dense-rhythms`, bar 13 of `stress-combined`) are therefore written into the .mscx (`mscxedit.py`) and re-saved by the app. In the .mscx a nested tuplet carries its ratio relative to its parent (the inner triplet is 3:2, not 9:4) and nesting is `<Tuplet>` ... `<endTuplet/>` pairs.
- MusicXML import turns `<segno/>`, `<coda/>`, `<sound dalsegno/tocoda/fine/dacapo>` into plain staff text, not Marker/Jump elements, so `jumps-markers` (and the markers in `stress-combined`) get real Marker/Jump measure elements by .mscx editing. In MuseScore the "To Coda" marker has `markerType` `coda` and the coda sign has `markerType` `codab`.
- Linked parts are written as separate score files under `Excerpts/` inside the .mscz; an excerpt element is tied to the master by `<linkedTo>` holding the master element's `<eid>`. `excerpts.py` builds this from the master and the app has to accept and re-save it, which is the check.
- Melismas are stored on the first syllable as `<ticks_f>` (a duration), not as a chain of notes; the MusicXML export writes a bare `<extend/>` on that one note only.
- Spanner end ticks are exclusive: a hairpin, 8va or pedal that ends at the first beat of bar N+1 is exported as ending in bar N. The spanner fixtures end their lines mid-bar so the exported bar equals the written bar.
